Complex numbers, finite fields and finite sets (Z3 5.x)

Source: R/z3v5.R
z3_v5_theories.Rd

Theories added in the Z3 5 series. Each needs z3r to be built against a Z3 that has it; otherwise the functions report the version they need.

Usage

z3_complex_sort(ctx)

z3_complex(re, im)

z3_real_part(z)

z3_imag_part(z)

z3_ff_sort(ctx, p)

z3_ff_size(sort)

z3_ff_add(...)

z3_ff_mul(...)

z3_ff_neg(x)

z3_ff_bitsum(...)

z3_finite_set_sort(element)

z3_fs_element_sort(sort)

z3_fs_empty(sort)

z3_fs_singleton(x)

z3_fs_union(s, t)

z3_fs_intersect(s, t)

z3_fs_difference(s, t)

z3_fs_member(x, s)

z3_fs_subset(s, t)

z3_fs_size(s)

z3_fs_range(lo, hi)

z3_fs_map(f, s)

z3_fs_filter(f, s)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

re, im

Real parts.

z

A complex expression.

p

A prime, as a string or whole number.

sort

A finite set or finite field sort.

...

Field elements.

x

An element.

element

Element sort.

s, t

Finite sets.

lo, hi

Int bounds.

f

An array-valued function.

Value

A z3_expr, a z3_sort, or for z3_ff_size() a string.

Details

  • Complex numbers (Z3 5.3.2): z3_complex_sort(ctx), z3_complex(re, im), z3_real_part(z), z3_imag_part(z). +, -, *, /, z3_sum(), z3_prod() and equality accept complex expressions, with Int and Real embedded exactly; R complex numbers such as 1+2i are literals under the usual double policy. Ordering is not defined for complex numbers.

  • Finite fields (Z3 5.3.0): z3_ff_sort(ctx, p) is the field of integers modulo the prime p (given as a string for large primes); z3_ff_add(), z3_ff_mul(), z3_ff_neg() and z3_ff_bitsum() (sum of the arguments weighted by successive powers of two) operate in it; z3_val() makes field elements. z3_ff_size() returns p.

  • Finite sets (Z3 5.0.0): z3_finite_set_sort(element) is the sort of finite sets with cardinality, unlike the array-based sets of z3_set_sort(). Operations: z3_fs_empty(), z3_fs_singleton(), z3_fs_union(), z3_fs_intersect(), z3_fs_difference(), z3_fs_member(), z3_fs_subset(), z3_fs_size() (an Int), z3_fs_range(lo, hi) (the integers from lo to hi), and the higher-order z3_fs_map(f, s) and z3_fs_filter(f, s) with array arguments such as z3_lambda(). z3_fs_element_sort() gives the element sort.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
if (z3_version_at_least("5.3.2")) {
  z <- z3_const(ctx, "z", z3_complex_sort(ctx))
  s <- z3_solver(ctx)
  z3_add(s, z3_real_part(z) == 3, z3_imag_part(z) == -4)
  z3_check(s)
}
#> [1] "sat"
if (z3_version_at_least("5.0.0")) {
  I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
  a <- z3_const(ctx, "a", z3_finite_set_sort(I))
  s <- z3_solver(ctx)
  z3_add(s, z3_fs_size(a) == 3, z3_fs_subset(a, z3_fs_range(z3_int_val(ctx, 1), 4)))
  z3_check(s)
}
#> [1] "unknown"
